newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India buys 135,000 T diesel in Feb top-up tender.
newsitem.headline: India buys 135,000 T diesel in Feb top-up tender.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) bought in a supplementary tender 135,000 tonnes of diesel for delivery in February, traders said on Monday.
All the diesel cargoes are for delivery to the west coast port of Kandla.
IOC also bought in the tender a 45,000-tonne cargo of SKO for delivery to the east-coast ports of Madras/Haldia.
IOC awarded two 45,000-tonne cargoes of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel to Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) at $1.59 and $1.64 per barrel over Middle East quotes on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis.
A 45,000-tonne cargo of 0.25-percent sulphur diesel was awarded to Italy's Agip at $3.10 premium over Middle East quotes c-and-f, traders said.
The kerosene cargo was awarded to Vitol at almost $3.00 premium to Middle East quotes c-and-f.
The results were in line with market expectations.
In its original tender for February deliveries, India bought 720,000 tonnes of diesel in 17 cargoes to both west and east coast ports.
In the original tender west-coast cargoes to Kandla were awarded between $24.00 and $27.00 per tonne above the high of Mediterranean quotes on a delivered basis.

Cargoes to Kandla and Goa were awarded between $26.00 and $28.00 per tonne over the high of Mediterranean quotes and east-coast cargoes were awarded between $27.00 and $29.00 per tonne above the high of Mediterranean quotes.
